Library Commands.name: CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary
Library Commands.description: Copies the given files, keeping their names, into a folder of the embedded library with one library operation. The target folder is created when it is missing. With overwriteIfExists an item of the same name in that folder is replaced.
Library Commands.method_code:
def copy_files_into_embedded_library(
    self,
    files: list[EmbeddedLibraryFile],
    target_folder: None | str = None,
    overwrite_if_exists: None | bool = None
) -> FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult:
    """
    Copies the given files, keeping their names, into a folder of the embedded library with
    one library operation. The target folder is created when it is missing. With
    overwriteIfExists an item of the same name in that folder is replaced.

    Args:
        files (list[EmbeddedLibraryFile]): The files to copy. Each keeps its file name
            inside the target folder.
        target_folder (None | str): Optional. The folder relative to the embedded library to
            copy the files into, for example 'Office/Doors'. Missing folders are created. By
            default the root of the embedded library.
        overwrite_if_exists (None | bool): Optional. When true, an item with the same name
            in the target folder is replaced. By default false.

    Returns:
        FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'files': files,
            'targetFolder': target_folder,
            'overwriteIfExists': overwrite_if_exists,
        }
    validated_params = CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibraryParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibrary",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    validated_response = TypeAdapter(CopyFilesIntoEmbeddedLibraryResult).validate_python(response_dict)
    return validated_response

Favorites Commands.name: ApplyFavoritesToElements
Favorites Commands.description: Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves or resizes the target element. For the hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. By default settings, classifications, categories and properties are all applied; each can be opted out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target (its ID, layer, an opening's width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line location, height and top link) that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied, so that e.g. only the library part or the wall type changes.
Favorites Commands.method_code:
def apply_favorites_to_elements(
    self,
    favorites_to_apply: list[FavoritesToApplyItem],
    apply_settings: None | bool = None,
    apply_classifications: None | bool = None,
    apply_categories: None | bool = None,
    apply_properties: None | bool = None,
    keep_fields: None | list[FavoriteKeepField] = None
) -> list[FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult]:
    """
    Apply the given favorites to existing elements. Only settings-type parameters are
    changed - geometry (position, floor, and dimensions such as a Wall's height) is left
    untouched, so applying a Favorite never moves or resizes the target element. For the
    hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-elements are
    not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own geometry. By default
    settings, classifications, categories and properties are all applied; each can be opted
    out of individually. keepFields lists fields of the target (its ID, layer, an opening's
    width, height and sill height, a Wall's reference line location, height and top link)
    that are copied back after the Favorite has been applied, so that e.g. only the library
    part or the wall type changes.

    Args:
        favorites_to_apply (list[FavoritesToApplyItem])
        apply_settings (None | bool): Whether to apply the Favorite's settings-type
            parameters (structure, materials, pens, etc. - never geometry). For the
            hierarchical types (Stair, Railing, Curtain Wall) the settings of the sub-
            elements are not applied, because they are inseparable from the Favorite's own
            geometry. Default is true.
        apply_classifications (None | bool): Whether to apply the Favorite's
            classifications. Default is true.
        apply_categories (None | bool): Whether to apply the Favorite's element categories
            (e.g. IFC categories). Default is true.
        apply_properties (None | bool): Whether to apply the Favorite's property values.
            Default is true.
        keep_fields (None | list[FavoriteKeepField]): Fields of the target element to keep:
            after the Favorite has been applied, they are copied back from the target as it
            was before, so only the Favorite's other settings (e.g. its library part or wall
            type) take effect. 'id' and 'layerIndex' apply to every element type; 'width',
            'height' and 'sillHeight' to a Window or Door ('width' and 'height' also to a
            Skylight); 'height', 'topOffset' and 'relativeTopStory' to a Wall or Column;
            'referenceLineLocation' to a Wall. A field the target's type does not have is
            ignored. To keep a Wall's or Column's top exactly as it was, keep 'height',
            'relativeTopStory' and 'topOffset' together - a kept 'height' alone is
            recomputed by Archicad while the Favorite's relativeTopStory links the top to a
            story. Default: nothing is kept.

    Returns:
        list[FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult]: A list of execution
            results.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'favoritesToApply': favorites_to_apply,
            'applySettings': apply_settings,
            'applyClassifications': apply_classifications,
            'applyCategories': apply_categories,
            'applyProperties': apply_properties,
            'keepFields': keep_fields,
        }
    validated_params = ApplyFavoritesToElementsParameters(**params_dict)

Navigator Commands.name: ChangeDrawingLink
Navigator Commands.description: Relinks a Drawing to a different source navigator item. Archicad has no in-place relink API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation). The new source view is made current before the Drawing is created (Archicad 27 or later), and the window and story that were active when the command started are restored afterwards; the view settings (zoom, layers, scale) shown in that window are not restored.
Navigator Commands.method_code:
def change_drawing_link(
    self,
    drawings_with_new_links: list[DrawingsWithNewLink]
) -> list[ElementIdArrayItem | ErrorItem]:

    API, so this recreates the Drawing against the new source and deletes the original - the
    returned elementId is a NEW guid, not the input one. The Drawing Title marker's own
    position is not preserved (undocumented Archicad limitation). The new source view is
    made current before the Drawing is created (Archicad 27 or later), and the window and
    story that were active when the command started are restored afterwards; the view
    settings (zoom, layers, scale) shown in that window are not restored.

    Args:
        drawings_with_new_links (list[DrawingsWithNewLink])

    Returns:
        list[ElementIdArrayItem | ErrorItem]: One result per input item. On success,
            elementId is the NEW Drawing's identifier - relinking necessarily replaces the
            element, it cannot keep the original guid.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {

        }
    validated_params = ChangeDrawingLinkParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(

Element Commands.name: DeleteElements
Element Commands.description: Deletes elements. The zones of the call are deleted before all the other elements, so an automatic zone deleted together with its bounding walls is gone before its boundary is; deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed polygon found' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it in Archicad. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) gets a failed execution result instead of being skipped silently.
Element Commands.method_code:
def delete_elements(
    self,
    elements: list[ElementIdArrayItem]
) -> list[FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult]:
    """
    Deletes elements. The zones of the call are deleted before all the other elements, so an
    automatic zone deleted together with its bounding walls is gone before its boundary is;
    deleting the boundary of an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's
    modal 'No closed polygon found' dialog, which blocks the command until someone clicks it
    in Archicad. Returns an execution result for each input element: an element that could
    not be deleted (for example because its layer is locked) gets a failed execution result
    instead of being skipped silently.

    Args:
        elements (list[ElementIdArrayItem]): The elements to delete. The zones among them
            are deleted before all the others, so an automatic zone deleted together with
            its bounding elements is gone before its boundary is. Deleting the boundary of
            an automatic zone without the zone itself can open Archicad's modal 'No closed
            polygon found around the clicked point' dialog, which blocks the command until
            someone clicks it in Archicad.

    Returns:
        list[FailedExecutionResult | SuccessfulExecutionResult]: A list of execution
            results.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {

    validated_params = DeleteElementsParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(

        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)

Application Commands.name: GetElementFromUser
Application Commands.description: Asks the designer to click an element in the current window and returns its id, its type and the clicked point. A click on empty space or on an element of a type not asked for asks again. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one until then; cancelling returns cancelled.
Application Commands.method_code:
def get_element_from_user(
    self,
    prompt: None | str = None,
    element_types: None | list[ElementType] = None
) -> GetElementFromUserResult:
    """
    Asks the designer to click an element in the current window and returns its id, its type
    and the clicked point. A click on empty space or on an element of a type not asked for
    asks again. Archicad waits for the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command
    queues behind this one until then; cancelling returns cancelled.

    Args:
        prompt (None | str): Shown in the control box while Archicad waits for the click.
            Single-byte text: the box takes a char field. Archicad's main thread waits for
            the click or for Escape, and every other JSON command queues behind this one
            until then.
        element_types (None | list[ElementType]): Only an element of one of these types is
            accepted. A click on empty space or on an element of another type asks for the
            click again. Default: any element.

    Returns:
        GetElementFromUserResult

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'prompt': prompt,
            'elementTypes': element_types,
        }
    validated_params = GetElementFromUserParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "GetElementFromUser",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    validated_response = GetElementFromUserResult.model_validate(response_dict)
    return validated_response

Graphic Override Commands.name: CreateGraphicalOverrideRule
Graphic Override Commands.description: Creates or overwrites a graphic override rule in a rule group: name, criterion XML, surface color and line pen. Needs Archicad 27 or later.
Graphic Override Commands.method_code:
def create_graphical_override_rule(
    self,
    name: str,
    rule_group_name: None | str = None,
    criterion_xml: None | str = None,
    surface_rgb: ColorRGB | None = None,
    line_pen_index: None | int = None,
    override_contours: None | bool = None
) -> GuidId:
    """
    Creates or overwrites a graphic override rule in a rule group: name, criterion XML,
    surface color and line pen. Needs Archicad 27 or later.

    Args:
        name (str): Name of the override rule. Rule names are unique in the project: an
            existing rule with this name is overwritten, in whichever rule group it is.
        rule_group_name (None | str): Rule group of a new rule, created when it does not
            exist. Default: 'Tapir'. An overwritten rule stays in its own group.
        criterion_xml (None | str): Optional criterion XML. Archicad only takes XML in its
            own format: read it from a rule made in the GUI with GetGraphicalOverrideRules
            and change the values. XML written from scratch is dropped without an error, and
            so is an empty one: the rule then applies to all elements.
        surface_rgb (ColorRGB | None): Optional color override of the cut and uncut
            surfaces. Components are in the 0..1 range.
        line_pen_index (None | int): Optional pen index override for lines, markers and
            texts. Only a positive index takes effect.
        override_contours (None | bool): Optional. If true, the contours of the overridden
            surfaces are recolored too.

    Returns:
        GuidId: The created or overwritten override rule.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    params_dict = {
            'name': name,
            'ruleGroupName': rule_group_name,
            'criterionXML': criterion_xml,
            'surfaceRGB': surface_rgb,
            'linePenIndex': line_pen_index,
            'overrideContours': override_contours,
        }
    validated_params = CreateGraphicalOverrideRuleParameters(**params_dict)
    response_dict = self._core.post_tapir_command(
        "CreateGraphicalOverrideRule",
        validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    validated_response = CreateGraphicalOverrideRuleResult.model_validate(response_dict)
    return validated_response.ruleId

            run label applies that style to every run; the other style fields leave the
            content as it is.

    Returns:

            results.

Navigator Tree Commands.name: API.RenameNavigatorItem
Navigator Tree Commands.description: Renames an existing navigator item by specifying either the name or the ID, or both.
Navigator Tree Commands.method_code:
def rename_navigator_item(
    self,
    navigator_item_id: NavigatorItemId,
    new_name: str | None = None,
    new_id: str | None = None
) -> None:
    """
    Renames an existing navigator item by specifying either the name or the ID, or both.

    Args:
        navigator_item_id (NavigatorItemId): The identifier of the navigator item to rename.
        new_name (str, optional): The new name for the navigator item.
        new_id (str, optional): The new ID for the navigator item.

    Raises:
        ArchicadAPIError: If the API returns an error response.
        RequestError: If there is a network or connection error.
        pydantic.ValidationError: If the parameters, or the API Response fail validation.
    """
    if not new_name and not new_id:
        raise ValueError("Either 'new_name' or 'new_id' (or both) must be provided.")

    if new_name and new_id:
        inner_model = RenameNavigatorItemByNameAndId(navigatorItemId=navigator_item_id, newName=new_name, newId=new_id)
    elif new_name:
        inner_model = RenameNavigatorItemByName(navigatorItemId=navigator_item_id, newName=new_name)
    else:
        inner_model = RenameNavigatorItemById(navigatorItemId=navigator_item_id, newId=new_id)

    validated_params = RenameNavigatorItemParameters(root=inner_model)
    self._core.post_command(
        "API.RenameNavigatorItem", validated_params.model_dump(mode='json', by_alias=True, exclude_none=True)
    )
    return None
